learningObjective: Compare two loop orderings of a naive GEMM for their locality behavior and identify which is legal and preferred on a row-major layout.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a row-major naive GEMM, the ikj loop ordering achieves unit-stride access to B (row-of-B) and C (row-of-C) in the innermost loop, giving better spatial locality and vectorizability than the ijk ordering, while being semantically equivalent for reduction into C[i,j].
conditions: FP non-associativity is treated as a numerical rather than a correctness constraint for the reduction over K.
nonImplications: Does not imply ikj is optimal; blocked and vectorized schedules outperform it.
Does not imply the same ordering is preferred on column-major layouts.

misconceptions.claim: Reordering GEMM loops changes numerical output enough to be treated as a semantics-changing transformation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP non-associativity is real but GEMM libraries and compilers treat different reduction orders as equivalent for correctness testing (within tolerance).

misconceptions.claim: The ikj ordering introduces a new loop-carried dependence that ijk did not have.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both orderings share the same reduction into C[i,j]; the dependence exists in both.

misconceptions.claim: Unit-stride writes cost more than unit-stride reads, so ijk (which strides through B) remains preferred on row-major.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both unit-stride reads and unit-stride writes benefit from cache locality; the read/write asymmetry is small and does not reverse the ordering preference.

misconceptions.claim: Loop reordering is a semantics-preserving transformation regardless of the underlying dependence structure.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Legality requires that no dependence in the loop nest is reversed by the interchange; some reorderings are illegal.

implementationFacts: BLAS libraries use blocked/vectorized inner kernels, not naive triple loops.
MLIR affine loop interchange checks dependences via access maps.
performanceScenarios: On x86 with SSE/AVX, ikj enables vectorization of the inner j loop over B[k,:] and C[i,:].
